subject: Post-demo: model-fit notes, benchmark links, and A/B test ops
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: evan.brooks@retailco.com, jason.liu@retailco.com; Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@retailco.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: model-fit notes, benchmark links, and A/B test ops

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and helpful context on the ranking edge cases you see in production. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Call highlights
- Primary objective: improve relevance for promotional and seasonal queries without regressing personalized CTR.
- Current baseline: in-production model (proprietary heuristic + simple BM25 re-ranker).
- Data constraints: 30d log window available, product metadata feed updated hourly, user history available for logged-in samples only.

Top model-fit takeaways from our initial bench (attached "rerank_benchmark_v1.xlsx")
- Candidate variants to validate: rw-rerank-v2-int8 (reduces cost), redwood/opt-2.7b-rerank (higher quality).
- Quick eval (holdout sample provided during call): rw-rerank-v2-int8 vs baseline: NDCG@10 +8.3% | MRR +6.9% (bootstrap, p<0.05). redwood/opt-2.7b-rerank shows slightly higher gains on long-tail queries but ~1.4x latency.
- Main quality concern: tail personalization and brand-query precision — we saw isolated regressions on queries with low click density.

Artifacts I shared (attached/links)
- rerank_benchmark_v1.xlsx — top-level metrics and per-query slices
- prompt_set_v2.jsonl — anonymized prompt/label samples for your data team
- Drive link: https://drive.redwood/reports/RDW-3891-benchmark

Proposed canary + A/B plan (high level)
1) Canary window: 1 week, 10% of traffic routed to canary model variant.
2) Variants: primary canary = rw-rerank-v2-int8; reserve option = redwood/opt-2.7b-rerank for a separate experiment if latency budget allows.
3) Key success metrics: NDCG@10 (holdout), relative CTR uplift on logged-in cohort, no >1% degradations on branded queries; SLO: p95 tail latency < 220ms.
4) Rollback rules: automatic rollback if NDCG drops >2% vs baseline or CTR drop >1.5% over 24h window.
5) Observability: per-query deltas, top-50 regressors list, and error/latency traces.

Ask of RetailCo (next 72h)
- Share a mapping file for product_id -> feature buckets (price band, promotion flag) and an export of 5k anonymized session traces (we can accept a sample).
- Confirm canary start date window (we suggested July 5).
- Approve access for our SRE to read-only observe the canary metrics dashboard.

I'll kick off a short internal ops plan (canary-ab-plan.md attached) and Rafael will follow up on infra config. Happy to hop on a quick sync if you want to walk through the benchmark sheet line-by-line.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Attachments: rerank_benchmark_v1.xlsx (sheet: summary), prompt_set_v2.jsonl (anonymized), canary-ab-plan.md
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@retailco.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: data-team@retailco.com, jason.liu@retailco.com
Date: 2026-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-fit notes, benchmark links, and A/B test ops

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary and great to see the NDCG/MRR lifts called out. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we circulate to our infrastructure team: 
1) Canary size: when you say 10% traffic, is that 10% of all search queries or 10% of sessions? We want to avoid skewing logged-in metrics.
2) Fallbacks: what's the expected behavior when a canary request times out or returns low-confidence?

I'll loop in our data folks (cc'd). We're inclined toward a July 5 start but want to confirm the rollback rules and monitoring endpoints. Also, can you confirm whether the prompt_set_v2 includes any user-identifying fields (it should not).

—Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Product, RetailCo
ev an.brooks@retailco.com
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: evan.brooks@retailco.com, data-team@retailco.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-fit notes, benchmark links, and A/B test ops

Great questions — quick answers inline: 
1) Traffic split: 10% of qualifying search requests (we recommend scoping to anonymous + logged-in sessions but analyzing logged-in separately). If you prefer, we can run session-based randomization; we typically do request-based for faster statistical power.
2) Fallbacks: default behavior is graceful fallback to baseline ranker on error/timeout. We also propose a conservative confidence threshold on the reranker score to trigger baseline. We'll include this in the canary runbook.
3) prompt_set_v2.jsonl is anonymized; it contains query text and item ids (hashed) only — no PII.

Operational details for the canary (proposed)\- Start: 2026-07-05 00:00 PT\- Traffic: 10% request split, holdout = 90%\- Primary KPIs: NDCG@10, logged-in CTR, avg latency (p95)\- Rollback: auto + manual check at 12h mark; auto if NDCG < -2% over 24h or CTR drop >1.5%

Next steps from my side: finalize the canary runbook and share the Doc link. Rafael — can you confirm infra and KV cache settings so the latency targets remain achievable?

Thanks,
Lauren

Quick internal note on ops and perf tuning: 
- Capacity: Redwood Dedicated pool has headroom for a 10% canary on the suggested endpoint—I'll reserve a burst slot for July 5–12.
- Latency controls: enable per-request KV cache for recent session vectors; use the int8 quantized variant (rw-rerank-v2-int8) for the main canary. If the team wants to try redwood/opt-2.7b-rerank, we should only run that on a separate 5% split due to higher latency.
- Monitoring: I'll provision the per-query delta dashboard and add automated alerts for the rollbacks you defined. Link: https://docs.redwood/ab-plans/RDW-3891-canary (will grant read-only to RetailCo ops).

Also flagged a task to ensure prompt_set_v2.jsonl uses hashed item ids only — Monica will run a quick PII sweep.
